title: Tughlaq Dynasty
capsule: The Tughlaq dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1320 to 1413, founded when Ghazi Malik seized the throne as Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq after killing the last Khalji sultan. Under Muhammad bin Tughluq (r. 1325–51) the sultanate reached its greatest territorial extent, briefly controlling most of the Indian subcontinent from the Deccan to Bengal, but his reign became synonymous with failed fiscal experiments including a debased token currency, forced capital relocation to Daulatabad, and mass rebellions. Firuz Shah Tughluq (r. 1351–88) stabilized the regime through extensive canal building and welfare works but could not reverse provincial fragmentation; Timur's devastating sack of Delhi in 1398 shattered what remained, and the last Tughluq sultan was deposed by Khizr Khan in 1413.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territorial extent is based on chronicle and inscription evidence; the outer limits of Tughluq control, particularly in the Deccan and Bengal, fluctuated rapidly and the geometry reflects a broad maximum extent rather than continuous administered territory.
